title: GOV-0003: badf init creates a Work Package with no demand record
problem:
## Observed
`badf init` (BADF-WP-0015) creates a work package, three G00 declarations, a dossier, a ledger and a registry entry from a six-field intent. `INTENT_REQUIRED` = intent, local_path, name, owner, repository, target. **No `issue` field.** The WP schema has no `issue`, `demand`, or `discovered_from` property at all.

## Expected (GITHUB_CONTROL_PLANE.md, adopted one WP after init shipped)
> No Work Package without an Issue or authorized demand.
An intake with no demand record is the exact pattern the doctrine forbids. `init` predates the doctrine; it is now non-compliant by construction.

## Evidence
`python3 -c "import scripts.badf_gate as g; print(sorted(g.INTENT_REQUIRED))"` → no issue. `schemas/work-package.schema.json` properties → no demand field.

## Unknowns
Whether the demand must be a GitHub Issue in **BADF's** repo, or may be an Issue in the target project's repo (PropTech has its own `[WP-NNNN]` admission control and its own issue space). Cross-repo demand binding is a design question, not a bug fix.

## Proposed work package
`BADF-WP-0018` — intent gains a required `demand` (an Issue URL or `repo#N`); WP schema gains `demand` bound to it; `init` refuses without it; the G00 dossier's `held_because` names the demand. The PropTech intake, when re-run, must cite a PropTech Issue.
